accepts.because: one conversational turn to be remembered verbatim -- ONE message carries ONE turn and its own provenance, so identity travels per message and two turns of one session may name two different people (GH #272); a closed session batch is no longer a shape this lane takes. `session_id` and `turn_id` travel as ingress context, `happened_at` on the hop for historical ingest. The provenance of the turn travels the same way and is NOT optional: `audience_set` (a JSON list of participants in affinity vocabulary, `*` alone meaning universal) and `channel` are required, and `speaker` for a user turn or `agent_id` for an assistant turn names who spoke -- absent, the stored `speaker` stays empty, never the role. Without an audience or a channel the turn is refused on `reject` -- who was present is the gate on every later read, it cannot be inferred afterwards, and a guessed audience is worse than a missing turn. The conditional pair `speaker`/`agent_id` is deliberately NOT in the `context` list above: that list names keys a caller must have promoted, and it cannot say `exactly one of these two`. So the list carries the four keys that are always required, and the fifth requirement lives here in prose -- visible rather than implied, and not something the declaration will ever check for you

a question against this memory. The five recall keys (recall_query, memory_tier, recall_as_of, recall_window_from, recall_window_to) come as context, always all five, empty string = unset. The asking round comes with them and is required: `audience_now` (a JSON list of who is present right now) and `channel` (where the question is being asked); `channel_open_history` is optional and defaults to '0', '1' saying this room shows joiners its history. Without `audience_now` or `channel` the question is refused on `reject` rather than answered unfiltered -- a recall without an audience is not a recall with an empty one. TWO MORE KEYS are read and neither is in the list above, for the same reason `channel_open_history` is not: the list names what a caller MUST have promoted, and a key with a default is not one of them. `session_id` scopes the session read -- the tier-0 leg reads the episodes of THAT session, and a question that names none reads a session called 'default', which in a live colony is nobody's. `recall_caller` is a REPLY-TO TOKEN this hive never reads: whatever a caller puts there rides through untouched and comes back on `hop.recall_caller` of the `bundle` and of a `reject`, which is how ONE hive serves SEVERAL askers and each of them gets ITS answer (GH #532). The token has to change compartment on the way out, and this hive is the only place that can do it for every caller at once: left on the hop it would not survive, because the `recall` cell forms its own hop and only context travels (GH #411), and a door guarded on context ALONE is condemned by crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh173_shipped_hive_contracts.rs AND ONE KEY IS READ TWICE (GH #536): `audience_now` is the audience gate's yardstick and, since the self leg, ALSO an IDENTITY -- its `member:`/`person:` tokens are the people this question is asked by, and a question in the first person ("what are my sons called?") anchors on them because it names nobody else. That is a second reading of a key the caller already promotes, not a new requirement: nothing has to be wired for it, and it widens no disclosure -- an anchor decides what is LOOKED UP, never what is seen, and every row it nominates is still measured against the same gate.

a block the front model decided to remember NOW, in the inline contract form; it is bound to the newest user turn of the caller session, so the session must be in the context. So must the provenance, on the same terms as `in_episode`: `audience_set` and `channel` are required and the block is refused on `reject` without them. The inline ingress writes facts directly, so it is the one lane where a missing audience would mint an untagged row without an episode ever refusing it first

a session that just ended, to be read WHOLE once (GH #300, ruling Q9). Per-turn annotation is blind in one direction -- the front model annotates the turn it has just answered and cannot know the turn after it -- so this lane is where a correction three turns later, a value the conversation only settled at the end and a claim the session itself retracted get sharpened. Nothing travels in the body: the lane names a session and the hive reads its own turns. The three keys are the same provenance every write lane of this hive demands, and for the same reason -- the pass proposes writes, so `session_id` says WHICH session is being closed, `audience_set` and `channel` say who was present and where, and a pass without them would mint sharpened rows nobody can filter afterwards. The shipped caller has all three already: `talky`'s `./session-keeper -> ./collector` close edge promotes exactly this set. What the pass did leaves on `close_report`; a pass that stopped leaves on `reject`

write this hive's remembered content OUT as a declared, versioned document (#243). Nothing travels on the hop: the lane names the whole memory. Sixteen parts leave on `dump`, one per content table, and the LAST one carries `hop.export_final = '1'` -- a document without that part is incomplete and is not a backup. Provenance travels with every row: the participant set, the room and the speaker are projected explicitly, because a column nobody selects is a column that never leaves the store

take ONE part of such a document into this RUNNING hive, idempotently. The part is the body; nothing else is needed and nothing is inferred. Applying the same part twice leaves the same state -- that is what makes the document a backup and a merge rather than only a birth seed. A part that lost a provenance column in transit is REFUSED on `reject` with nothing written: an imported row whose participant set did not survive is a row that may be told to anyone

emits.because: the answer to a question: the recalled material, fused and ranked, for whoever asked. WHICH of them asked is `hop.recall_caller`, carried back off `context.recall_caller` exactly as the asking round put it there and empty when it put nothing (GH #532). This hive serves one member and more than one asker inside it -- a conversation surface and a reasoning core today -- and the token is the only thing in the answer that tells them apart. It is handed back, never read and never interpreted

something this hive was sent and would not take -- a block it cannot bind, a half window it will not guess at, a turn or a question whose audience or channel is missing (`hop.reject_reason` is then 'missing_audience' or 'missing_channel'). Since 2.3.1 it also carries what this hive's OWN STORE would not do: a lane whose read or write came back refused stops there and says so, with `hop.reject_reason` = 'store_refused', `hop.store_error` carrying the store's own `error_code` and `hop.store_operation` naming the op that was refused (GH #343) -- including the nightly consolidation, which has no caller of its own and reports on this lane rather than nowhere. The code rides in `store_error` rather than inside `reject_reason` on purpose: the store's code list is OPEN (`invalid_input`, `query_timeout`, `write_denied`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_column`, `constraint_violation`, `sql_error`, ...), and a reason enum that had to grow with it would turn the next new code into a failed emit. The body says which and why. Drain it: undrained, nobody ever learns the memory was not written and the caller waits for a bundle that never comes. A refusal on the RECALL lane carries `hop.recall_caller` home exactly as a bundle does (GH #532): the asker that cannot be told its question failed is the one that waits longest

what the close pass did with one closed session (GH #300, ruling Q9): how many turns it read, what it sharpened and what it left alone. It is the ONLY positive signal the lane has -- the pass writes through the inline ingress, which answers nobody, so without this the caller cannot tell a pass that ran and changed nothing from a pass that never ran at all. Drain it: undrained, the pass costs one strong-model call per session and reaches nobody, which is the same disease as an undrained export

the transfer lane's output: `hop.dump_kind == 'export_part'` is one part of the exported document (`hop.export_part` of `hop.export_of`, `hop.export_final` marking the last), `hop.dump_kind == 'import_receipt'` says what one applied part wrote (`hop.rows_written`). Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'dump'` edge -- an edge that also tests `dump_kind` reads as no drain under the required_drains probe. Undrained, an export runs and reaches nobody

required_drains.because: since 2.1.0 a turn without a participant set or without a channel is REFUSED rather than written (#244) -- undrained, the refusal is silent and the caller believes a memory was kept that never existed, which is the one failure this gate exists to prevent
a block this hive refuses leaves on the reject lane -- undrained, nobody ever learns the memory was not written and the caller waits for a bundle that never comes
a question this hive will not answer -- a half window it will not guess at -- leaves on the reject lane; undrained, the asker waits for a bundle that will never arrive

the report is the pass's only positive signal -- it writes through the inline ingress, which answers nobody. Undrained, one strong-model call per closed session runs, costs money and reaches nobody, and nothing anywhere says whether it ever ran
a pass this hive stopped -- the store refused the session read above all -- leaves here; undrained, a close pass that did nothing looks exactly like one that sharpened everything it found
the export IS the dump lane -- wired without it, the walk runs, reads the whole store and delivers the document to nobody
an export that aborts mid-walk (the store refused a read) has already emitted parts; undrained, the caller keeps a partial document that looks complete
the receipt of an applied part is the only positive signal an import has -- undrained, nobody ever learns whether a transfer landed
a part this hive will not take -- one whose audience did not survive the transfer above all -- leaves here; undrained, a refused transfer looks exactly like a successful one

description.purpose: Scope marker of the memory hive: bundles the durable store and the write/recall/extraction/consolidation lanes of one MEMBER's memory behind ITS OWN PATH (ADR-0002 E1 -- agents are lenses on it, a second agent of the same member inherits what that member knows). `params.ports` is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here; a caller names the hive and a lane on `hop.route`. The transfer lane (#243) carries the content OUT as a versioned document and back IN to a running hive, so a memory is an asset with an identity of its own rather than a side effect of one deployment. The consolidation lane carries two model roles: the dreamer writes the change narrative, the judge decides identity for the nightly canonicalisation round.
description.use_when: Instantiate once per member; wire the lanes at the hive path in the same mutation. Every write lane needs the provenance of the turn on its ingress context (audience_set, channel, and speaker/agent_id), every read lane the asking round (audience_now, channel).
description.not_in_scope: No agent logic, no conversation state, no routing for the parent scope — the hive only carries its internal graph.
description.contract_in: Six lanes, all at the hive path. in_episode -- remember this turn. in_query -- answer this question. in_remember -- take this block now (inline). in_close_pass -- this session is over, read it whole once. in_export -- write the remembered content out as a document. in_import -- take one part of such a document in, idempotently. Which cell serves a lane is this hive's business.
description.contract_out: Four lanes, out of the hive path. bundle -- the answer to a question. close_report -- what the close pass did with one session. dump -- the transfer document, part by part, and the receipt of an applied part. reject -- something this hive would not take; the body says which and why.
